text: Lesson 25 left Patient Scheduling's CMDB record accurate, but none of that survives on its own. A CMDB without governance drifts exactly like any other unowned system — someone decommissions a server without updating its CI, and six months later the whole capstone is the stale, untrustworthy record leadership asked to avoid back in Lesson 23. This lesson is the plan that keeps that from happening.

Every layer gets a specific, accountable owner, not a department. The Director of Patient Access owns the Patient Scheduling Business Service. The Infrastructure Team Lead for Clinical Systems owns the Technical Service underneath it. The Windows server team, the database administration team, and the network team each steward their own CIs — SCHED-APP-01 and 02, SCHED-SQL-01, and SCHED-LB-01.

One review frequency isn't enough, because different problems surface at different speeds. Monthly, the Technical Service Owner checks the Health Dashboard for this service specifically. Quarterly, both owners confirm the CSDM mapping still reflects what's actually running. Annually, every CI gets fully re-certified — still needed, still correctly classified, still correctly related — with anything that fails flagged for decommission.

Beyond the one-time check in Lesson 25, four things get watched on an ongoing basis: completeness trending flat or better, the duplicate count staying at zero, any CI going stale with no recent Discovery scan, and any CI turning up orphaned with no relationships at all — almost always a sign something was added outside this governance process.

This course has built toward one discipline: knowing precisely and currently what infrastructure exists and how it relates to the services it supports. The next course, Security and Access Controls, depends on exactly that discipline — an asset-based access policy scoped to who can touch SCHED-APP-01 or query SCHED-SQL-01 is only as reliable as the ownership and relationship data this capstone just built.
Get the CMDB wrong, and security policy built on top of it is wrong in exactly the same way. That's where this path goes next: ServiceNow Security and Access Controls, course ten of fourteen.
